Lisbon remains one of Western Europe's most affordable capitals, and a little planning goes a long way toward stretching your budget further.

## Getting around

The Viva Viagem card covers trams, metro, buses, and even the funiculars, and a day pass costs a fraction of what a single taxi ride would run you.

## Where to eat

Skip the touristy spots along the main squares and look instead for a "tasca" — a small family-run restaurant serving a fixed daily menu, often for less than the cost of a coffee and pastry elsewhere.

## Free things to do

Many of Lisbon's miradouros, or viewpoints, are completely free and offer some of the best sunset views in the city. The Miradouro da Senhora do Monte and Miradouro de Santa Catarina are both worth the walk uphill.

Accommodation is where most budget travelers save the most, and Lisbon's hostel scene is strong enough that even the highly rated options rarely require booking more than a few weeks in advance outside of peak summer months.
